title: Manufacturer secures £1.7m bridge for West Yorkshire site
summary:
Recognise Bank has provided a £1,697,500 bridging loan to enable a manufacturing company to acquire two industrial units in West Yorkshire. The borrower, a manufacturer with more than 35 years of trading history, produces coatings, adhesives, elastomers and moulded rubber products.

title: Bridging lender facilitates below-market property deal
summary:
Bridging lender Somo has completed a second charge loan enabling a borrower to acquire a buy-to-let property valued at £500,000 for £350,000, whilst simultaneously clearing six months of mortgage arrears. The transaction involved a seller relocating overseas who required a quick sale.

title: Nearly half of unsafe cladding buildings await remediation
summary:
Almost nine years after the Grenfell Tower fire, 47% of buildings identified with unsafe cladding have yet to begin or complete remediation works. Of 4,411 residential buildings over 11 metres tall, only 1,672 have finished remediation work.

title: Fine & Country updates sales boards for 25th anniversary
summary:
Fine & Country has introduced redesigned 'For Sale' boards across its network as part of a brand refresh coinciding with the estate agency's 25th anniversary in 2026. The updated boards incorporate the company's recently revised logo and have been deployed across its network of more than 300 offices internationally.

title: TPFG awards share options to executives tied to performance
summary:
The Property Franchise Group has granted share options to senior executives including CEO Gareth Samples as part of a three-year performance-linked incentive scheme. The awards cover the period to December 2028 following the company's 39% profit increase last year.

title: Salisbury Novichok property listed at £114,000
summary:
The three-bedroom property at the centre of the 2018 Salisbury Novichok poisoning incident has been listed for sale at £114,000 as shared ownership. The listing includes disclosure of the property's involvement in the nerve agent incident.

title: Property listing removed after Nazi items visible in tour
summary:
A property listing in Lincolnshire has been removed from major portals after a virtual tour revealed Nazi-era memorabilia displayed inside the home. The incident has raised questions about pre-listing vetting procedures in the industry.

title: Second home markets face price falls and ownership decline
summary:
House prices have declined in 20 of the 25 local authorities with the highest concentration of second homes in England by the first quarter of 2026, according to wealth manager Rathbones. The number of second homes in England has decreased by 12,000 since 2024, representing a 4.3% decline.

title: Developer secures £18m refinancing for Edinburgh student scheme
summary:
Student accommodation developer Danehurst has completed an £18 million refinancing of The Pepper Mill, a 155-studio purpose-built student accommodation development in Bonnington, Edinburgh. The deal comes as the city faces a shortfall exceeding 18,000 student beds.

title: Landlords warned over insurance gaps as regulations tighten
summary:
Landlords are failing to adequately disclose property and tenant details to insurers, creating potential coverage gaps that could prove costly when claims are made. Underinsurance remains a significant issue, with properties potentially left exposed if not insured for their true value.
